title: VLN-CE Isaac Dataset
description: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments dataset for Isaac Lab simulation. This dataset contains navigation episodes with natural language instructions for training embodied AI agents.

episodes.description: List of navigation episodes, each containing a complete navigation task

Episode.description: A single navigation episode representing one complete navigation task from start to goal

episode_id.description: Unique identifier for this navigation episode within the dataset

scene_id.description: Path to the 3D scene file (USD/GLB format). Format: 'provider/scene_identifier' where provider can be 'mp3d' (Matterport3D), 'Urbansim', etc.

start_position.description: Starting 3D position of the robot in world coordinates (meters). Format: [x, y, z]

start_rotation.description: Starting orientation of the robot as a quaternion. Format: [x, y, z, w] following the Hamilton convention (scalar-last)

geodesic_distance.description: Shortest path distance from start position to goal position in meters (ignoring obstacles)

goals.description: List of goal specifications. Typically contains one goal, but can support multiple goals for complex tasks

instruction.description: Natural language navigation instruction in English describing the path from start to goal. Instructions are human-written and describe landmarks, directions, and stopping conditions
instruction.example: Exit the bedroom and turn left. Walk straight passing the gray couch and stop near the rug.

reference_path.description: High-level reference path as a sequence of waypoints. These are key positions along the optimal path, typically 4-10 waypoints that define the general trajectory

gt_locations.description: Ground truth trajectory as a dense sequence of 3D positions. Sampled at regular intervals (typically 0.25m steps) along the optimal path. Used for imitation learning and trajectory evaluation

gt_steps.description: Total number of forward steps in the ground truth trajectory. Does not include turning actions

Goal.description: Defines a goal location and success criteria for navigation

radius.description: Success radius in meters. The robot is considered to have reached the goal if it gets within this distance of the goal position

Position3D.description: 3D position in world coordinates. Format: [x, y, z] in meters

episodes.instruction: Walk straight ahead, stop at the black iron gate, then turn right. Pass through the gate, go past the bench, and stop next to the black trash can.
